thread:
Maya: Quick proposal: expose a 'quota advisory' signal from runtime when capacity is degraded. Two approaches: (1) 429 + subcode + header, or (2) 200 + advisory field + header. Want platform/SDK/console input.

Sam: 429 is clear but SDKs + HTTP clients auto-retry. Could cause load amplification.

Kevin: We could use a special 429 subcode and header so SDKs can special-case it. Example: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Quota: advisory
Retry-After: 8
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"quota.advisory","message":"advisory: reduced throughput","hint":"lower concurrency or wait 8s","code":"QUOTA_ADVISORY"}
```

Kevin: That gives machines a strong signal and lets SDKs opt-out of retrying.

Alisha: Concern: some customers chain Redwood calls through proxies and expect 200s (caching, logging). Returning 429 might break third-party infra or trigger false alarms in monitoring. Also many generic HTTP clients treat 429 as retryable by default.

Maya: Variant: return 200 but include header + top-level advisory field so SDKs/apps can react without automatic retries: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Quota: advisory
Content-Type: application/json

{"result": {...}, "quota_advisory": "reduced", "quota_action": "suggest-reduce-concurrency"}
```

Maya: Runtime win: avoids retry storms. App win: explicit field to surface in UI. Downsides: semantic misuse of 200 for throttling.

Sam: Telemetry point: we should emit span tags either way: quota.mode=(advisory|strict), route.policy=degrade, quota.surface=on. That will let console show per-route advisory rates.

Kevin: Also suggest adding a short machine-readable header like X-Redwood-Quota-Code: advisory.v1 so we can iterate.

Alisha: For console UX: show a pink/orange banner: "Advisory capacity active on this route — recommended mitigations" with a runbook link and toggle to suppress advisories org-wide. Need copy and per-route counters.

opsbot: deploy-bot: feature-flag rollout queued for quota_advisory_surface_v1 -> staging (build 2026.03.21.4)

Sam: My leaning: prefer 429 with a distinct advisory code if we also ship SDK changes to avoid auto-retry. That preserves HTTP semantics for operators.

Maya: Proposal hybrid: default API returns 429+advisory for direct API calls. For customers behind caching/proxy layers we offer a compatibility header mode via a runtime flag `advisory_as_header` that returns 200+header when enabled per org. Means we support both ecosystem needs.

Kevin: SDK plan: add `treatQuotaAdvisory` option (default: false). If enabled, SDK will surface advisory to app and not auto-retry; if disabled SDK will perform a capped backoff. Also publish migration guide.

Alisha: Rollout plan: canary to internal orgs (3 orgs) for 48h, telemetry check: advisory.ratio < 5% and no retry storms. Then 10% customer orgs for 72h. Expose console toggle `quota_advisory_surface_v1`.

Maya: Telemetry keys we agreed on: `quota.mode`, `quota.surface`, `route.policy`, `quota.advisory_code`. Console metrics: per-route advisory count, advisory->retry correlation, advisory->error/regression signal.

Kevin: I'll open the API PR for 429 + X-Redwood-Quota + X-Redwood-Quota-Code. Also add unit tests for header presence and JSON shape.

Maya: Alisha owns console copy + dashboard queries. Sam will coordinate SDK changes. I'll handle runtime flags and rollout gating.

Alisha: I'll draft banner text and queries (grafana/trace) and share. Ping if telemetry names shift.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for quota_advisory_surface_v1 -> prod-canary (3 orgs)

Maya: Decision captured: default API signal = 429 with `QUOTA_ADVISORY` code + headers; compatibility path = 200+header via org runtime flag; SDK opt-in controls to avoid silent retries; telemetry + console badges + runbook. Thanks all :thumbsup:
